indexPrompt.ts-changes-when-growth-speeds-up: A 5-nearest-neighbor regressor predicts the next day-to-day change in electricity demand from the last 14 changes, and its forecast is today's demand plus the predicted change. In the test month demand grows by about 0.8 units a day, faster than over any two weeks of the two training years, so how do its one-step forecasts behave?
indexPrompt.ts-differencing-a-flat-series: A series is a constant plus independent noise, and a model forecasts its first differences by least squares. Find the correlation between neighboring differences, the mean squared error of the one-lag forecast, and how that error shrinks as the number of fitted lags grows.
indexPrompt.ts-features-three-days-ahead: A bakery forecasts the loaves it will sell on day t on the evening of day t minus 3, after that day's sales are counted. Its table has one row per day in date order with a column y for loaves sold, and the model is trained on rows indexed by the target day t. Which single pandas expression gives a feature summarizing a week of recent sales using only sales already known on the evening of day t minus 3?
indexPrompt.ts-mape-on-a-quiet-day: A bakery sells a specialty loaf whose daily sales swing widely, and two models forecast five test days, one of which sold only two loaves. Compute each model's MAE and MAPE, then say which metric a baker should choose when every loaf baked and not sold and every customer turned away costs the same.
indexPrompt.ts-mase-against-last-year: A ski rental shop records its revenue each quarter, in thousands of dollars, for three years. For year 4 the model forecasts 26, 39, 36 and 48 while the actual revenue is 27, 41, 34 and 49. Compute the model's MASE on year 4 against the seasonal naive scale, then find the scale a teammate used to report a MASE of 0.11 and say why that scale flatters the model.
indexPrompt.ts-naive-error-around-the-clock: An hourly load series is a daily sine cycle plus independent noise, and it may also drift up by a fixed amount each hour. Derive the mean squared error of the naive forecast, which repeats the last value, and of seasonal naive, which repeats the value from the same hour a day earlier, then compare them horizon by horizon.
indexPrompt.ts-the-constant-mape-prefers: A grader scores forecasts by MAPE, so find the one constant forecast it rewards most, derive what that constant is in general, and compute it for daily sales of 4, 5, 10, 20 and 40. Then explain what a model trained on squared error will score under this grader and what change to training fixes it.
indexPrompt.ts-two-steps-two-ways: A standardized series has lag-1 correlation 0.5 and lag-2 correlation 0.6. Forecast two steps ahead by fitting a one-step model and applying it twice, and separately by fitting the two-step target directly, then compare the two mean squared errors.
indexPrompt.ts-when-scale-is-the-signal: A plant records 400 vibration readings per pump sample. A worn bearing makes the same hum as a healthy one but its whole trace is about three times as large, and the hum can start anywhere in the sample. Which preprocessing step leaves a classifier with nothing to tell worn pumps from healthy ones?
indexPrompt.ts-windows-for-a-store-chain: A grocery chain has one year of daily sales, days 0 to 364, for each of its 40 stores. A model reads 28 consecutive days of one store and predicts that store's next 7 days, and it is scored on days 335 to 364. How many windows keep every scored day out of the training targets?
